:::{#exm-condition-number-gram}
#### Squaring the condition number

For the [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{A}$ from @exm-matrix-condition-number,
compare $\condnum(\matr{A})$ with $\condnum(\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A})$:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: condition-number-gram-r
#| code-fold: false
gram_cng <- crossprod(a_mcn)
kappa_a_cng <- sv_mcn[1] / sv_mcn[2]
sv_gram_cng <- svd(gram_cng)$d
sv_gram_cng[1] / sv_gram_cng[2]
kappa_a_cng^2
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: condition-number-gram-python
#| code-fold: false
gram_cng = a_mcn.T @ a_mcn
kappa_a_cng = sv_mcn[0] / sv_mcn[1]
sv_gram_cng = np.linalg.svd(gram_cng, compute_uv=False)
print(sv_gram_cng[0] / sv_gram_cng[1])
print(kappa_a_cng ** 2)
```

:::

The [condition number](#def-matrix-condition-number) of $\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{A}$ is `r sprintf("%.0f", sv_gram_cng[1] / sv_gram_cng[2])`,
and $\condnum(\matr{A})^2 =$ `r sprintf("%.0f", kappa_a_cng^2)`,
as @thm-condition-number-gram says.

:::
